title: Venthondiyar Clan Heritage Documentary
intro: An AI-assisted historical heritage documentary that brings a family’s 250+ years of history to the screen.
overview: The Venthondiyar Clan documentary tells the story of one family across more than two and a half centuries. Very little of that history exists as photographs or film, so the visual world had to be rebuilt.

Using research as the source of truth and AI image and video generation as the camera, the film reconstructs places, people and moments that could not be filmed, held together by narration and a consistent cinematic look.
objective: Preserve a family’s history in a form future generations will actually watch: a cinematic documentary that feels grounded and respectful rather than synthetic.
approach: Every scene started from research, not from a prompt. Historical details decided costume, architecture and setting before any image was generated.
A fixed visual language (palette, lighting direction, lens feel) was defined up front and reused across every generation so the film reads as one piece instead of a collage of AI clips.
process: Gathering the family history, names, places and periods.
Shaping the history into chapters and a narration script.
Breaking each chapter into scenes and shots.
Generating key images and locking the visual style.
Animating approved frames into cinematic shots.
Cutting to the voice-over, adding music, sound and grade.
media: Before / after: research reference vs final frame
results: Results, screenings or audience response will be added here once verified.

title: Brandstep Commercial Campaigns
intro: Advertisements and product videos created for clients of Brandstep Digital Marketing Agency, from product storytelling to final delivery.
overview: At Brandstep I edit and lead the production of commercial videos for the agency’s clients: product films, ad creatives and social content built to stop the scroll and sell.

Featured here is work for Zubi Candy, a confectionery brand, including product films for its jelly lolly and teddy jelly lines. More client campaigns will be added as assets are cleared for public use.
objective: Make each product look as appealing as possible in the first seconds, communicate the offer clearly, and deliver ad-ready versions for each platform on deadline.
approach: Product first: lighting, texture and motion that make the product the hero of every frame.
Short, clear structure (hook, product, offer, call to action) cut in versions for each placement, then refined through client feedback rounds.
process: Hook ideas and the visual direction for the product.
Footage, product shots and AI-assisted visuals where useful.
Final exports in every required format.
results: Campaign results will be added here only when verified by the client or the agency.

title: AI Filmmaking Experiments
intro: Cinematic visuals and short video experiments made with generative AI, exploring how far AI tools can be directed like a real camera crew.
overview: These experiments are where I test new AI tools and techniques before using them on client or documentary work.
Each piece is treated like a film shoot: a concept, a look, a shot list, then prompting and iteration until the frames feel directed rather than generated.
objective: Build a reliable, repeatable AI filmmaking workflow with consistent characters, intentional camera movement and cinematic light.
approach: Start with strong still frames, then animate them. Camera moves, lens and lighting are written into every prompt the way a cinematographer would brief a crew.
Characters are kept consistent through reference images and a fixed description, so the same person survives from shot to shot.
process: A mood, a story beat or a technique to test.
Reference frames for palette, light and lens.
Shot-by-shot prompts with camera and lighting direction.
Fixing continuity, faces and motion artefacts.
Assembling, scoring and grading the final piece.
results: Experiment notes and outcomes will be added as each piece is published.

title: Faith & Community Creative Projects
intro: Event branding, posters, promotional videos and storytelling for church and youth communities, including MULTITUDE: The Youth Carol Clash.
overview: Alongside agency work, I create for my faith community, where the goal is participation and togetherness rather than sales.

The featured project is MULTITUDE: The Youth Carol Clash, a youth carol-singing competition presented by St. Joseph Youth, Selaiyur (Tambaram Vicariate). The name draws on Luke 2:13, the multitude of the heavenly host praising God.
objective: Give the event a memorable identity and promotion that brings youth groups across the vicariate to take part.
approach: Start from the meaning: a name rooted in scripture that also sounds like a modern event brand.
Carry one visual identity across posters, social posts and video so every touchpoint feels like the same event.
process: What the event is for and who it should reach.
Choosing a name with meaning: MULTITUDE (Luke 2:13).
Logo, colours and type for the event.
media: Other church event posters and community videos
results: Participation and event outcomes will be added once confirmed.

title: Creative Experiments / Visual Lab
intro: A space for experimental designs, motion graphics, AI visuals and personal creative explorations, where new ideas get tested before they reach client work.
overview: Not every idea starts with a brief. The Visual Lab collects the personal work that keeps my craft sharp: motion tests, typography experiments, AI visuals and design studies.
This page grows over time as new experiments are added.
objective: Keep learning in public, and build a library of techniques that make client and documentary work better.
approach: Small, fast experiments, each testing one idea: a transition, a type treatment, a lighting style or a new AI tool.
The best results become techniques in my production workflow.
process: One question or technique to explore.
Publish it here and on social media.
